title: Relative diagonals of algebraic stack morphisms are representable and locally of finite type
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Use algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and fibred groupoids, morphisms, representability and 2-fibre products [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be any morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$. Its relative diagonal $\Delta_f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, $x\mapsto(x,x,\mathrm{id}_{f(x)})$, is representable by algebraic spaces and locally of finite type. Explicitly, for every $S$-scheme $T$ and morphism $t:T\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, the 2-fibre product $T\times_{t,\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X,\Delta_f}\mathcal X$ is equivalent over $T$ to an algebraic space locally of finite type over $T$. Local finite type on algebraic spaces is tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 04XS (lemma-properties-diagonal), parts (1) and (2), including the scheme-test formulation in its proof.

proof.text: Fix $t:T\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$. The fibre-product convention gives $t=(x,x',\alpha)$ with $x,x'\in\mathcal X(T)$ and $\alpha:f(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}f(x')$. Put $I=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X,T}(x,x')$ and $J=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y,T}(f(x),f(x'))$. By [lem-sfb-stack-isom-space-locally-finite-type], both are algebraic spaces over $T$, and $I\to T$ is locally of finite type. Applying $f$ to arrows gives a $T$-map $q:I\to J$, and $\alpha$ gives a section $a:T\to J$. These are natural transformations because $f$ commutes with pullback.

Let $P=T\times_{a,J,q}I$, an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. We identify $P$ with the 2-pullback $E=T\times_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X}\mathcal X$. For a scheme $H\to T$, an object of $E(H)$ is $(z,u:z\xrightarrow{\sim}x_H,v:z\xrightarrow{\sim}x'_H)$ with $f(v)=\alpha_H f(u)$. Send it to $\beta=vu^{-1}$, so $f(\beta)=\alpha_H$; these are precisely the elements of $P(H)$. Conversely send such a $\beta$ to $(x_H,1,\beta)$. An arrow between triples is $h:z\to z'$ satisfying $u'h=u$ and $v'h=v$. It exists exactly when $vu^{-1}=v'(u')^{-1}$ and then equals $(u')^{-1}u$. Hence each fibre over $\beta$ is equivalent to the singleton groupoid. The two constructions commute with restriction in $H$, and $u$ supplies their natural inverse isomorphism on triples. They therefore give an equivalence $E\simeq P$ over $T$, with the projection identified with $P\to T$.

The composite $I\xrightarrow{q}J\to T$ is the structure morphism $I\to T$, already locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-space-lft-cancellation] to these three algebraic spaces (regarding $T$ as its represented algebraic space). It follows that $q$ is locally of finite type. This cancellation requires no separatedness or finite-type hypothesis on $J\to T$.

The map $P\to T$ is the base change of $q$ along $a$. The algebraic-space case of [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus] preserves local finite type under arbitrary base change and identifies that notion with the ordinary etale-chart notion for algebraic spaces. Thus $P\to T$ is locally of finite type. Step 2 now proves the explicit scheme-test assertion for every $T,t$. The definition of representability by algebraic spaces therefore gives representability of $\Delta_f$, and the same scheme tests give its local finite type, with exactly the chart convention in the statement.
